# truefoundry_agent (Resource)

Manages a TrueFoundry-hosted AI Gateway agent (`truefoundry-agent` manifest) via `PUT /api/svc/v1/agents`. Every update creates a new immutable agent version on the control plane. Self-hosted agents are managed with `truefoundry_remote_agent`; agent skills and the legacy `agent` manifest type are not supported. Existing agents can be imported by their name, e.g. `terraform import truefoundry_agent.example my-agent`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A TrueFoundry-hosted agent using a gateway model, an MCP server, and
# structured output.
resource "truefoundry_agent" "support_triage" {
  name        = "support-triage"
  description = "Triages inbound support tickets and suggests a severity"

  model = {
    name = "azure-main/gpt-5-mini"
    params = {
      max_tokens       = 4096
      reasoning_effort = "medium"
    }
  }

  instructions = "Triage the ticket. The product area is {{product}}."

  variables = {
    product = {
      default_value = "app"
      description   = "Product area of the ticket"
    }
  }

  mcp_servers = [
    {
      name                       = truefoundry_mcp_server.wiki.name
      enable_tools               = ["@all"]
      require_approval_for_tools = ["@write", "@destructive"]
    },
  ]

  response_format = {
    type = "json_schema"
    json_schema = {
      name = "triage-result"
      schema = jsonencode({
        type = "object"
        properties = {
          severity = { type = "string" }
          summary  = { type = "string" }
        }
      })
      strict = true
    }
  }

  config = {
    iteration_limit    = 50
    ask_user_questions = { enabled = true }
    context_management = {
      compaction = {
        enabled                     = true
        compaction_threshold_tokens = 50000
      }
    }
  }

  collaborators = [
    {
      subject = "team:everyone"
      role_id = "agent-access"
    },
  ]

  tags = {
    team = "support"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `description` (String) Human-readable description of what the agent does.
- `model` (Attributes) The gateway model the agent runs on. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--model))
- `name` (String) Name of the agent (3-32 characters, lowercase alphanumeric and single hyphens). Changing it replaces the agent.

### Optional

- `collaborators` (Attributes Set) Subjects with a role on this agent. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collaborators))
- `config` (Attributes) Runtime configuration of the agent. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config))
- `instructions` (String) System instructions for the agent. May reference variables as {{name}}.
- `mcp_servers` (Attributes List) Gateway MCP servers the agent may use, referenced by name. They must exist on the same tenant. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mcp_servers))
- `response_format` (Attributes) Constrains the agent's final response. Omitted means free-form text. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--response_format))
- `sample_inputs` (Attributes List) Example inputs shown in the agent playground. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--sample_inputs))
- `skills` (Attributes List) Agent skills attached to the agent, referenced by their FQN. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--skills))
- `tags` (Map of String) Free-form key-value tags on the agent.
- `variables` (Attributes Map) Template variables usable in the instructions as {{name}}. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--variables))

### Read-Only

- `fqn` (String) Fully qualified name of the agent, e.g. my-tenant:agent:my-agent.
- `id` (String) Control plane ID of the agent.

<a id="nestedatt--model"></a>
### Nested Schema for `model`

Required:

- `name` (String) Gateway model name in provider-account/model form, e.g. my-account/gpt-5-mini.

Optional:

- `params` (Attributes) Inference parameters passed to the model. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--model--params))

<a id="nestedatt--model--params"></a>
### Nested Schema for `model.params`

Optional:

- `max_tokens` (Number) Maximum number of tokens the model may generate per turn.
- `parallel_tool_calls` (Boolean) Allow the model to call multiple tools in parallel.
- `reasoning_effort` (String) Reasoning effort for reasoning models, e.g. low, medium, or high.
- `temperature` (Number) Sampling temperature.
- `top_k` (Number) Top-k sampling cutoff.
- `top_p` (Number) Nucleus sampling probability mass.



<a id="nestedatt--collaborators"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collaborators`

Required:

- `role_id` (String) Role to assign, e.g. agent-access or agent-manager.
- `subject` (String) Subject FQN, e.g. user:jane@example.com or team:everyone.


<a id="nestedatt--config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config`

Optional:

- `ask_user_questions` (Attributes) Let the agent ask the user clarifying questions. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--ask_user_questions))
- `context_management` (Attributes) How the agent keeps its context within limits. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--context_management))
- `dynamic_sub_agents` (Attributes) Let the agent spawn sub-agents dynamically. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--dynamic_sub_agents))
- `generative_ui` (Attributes) Let the agent render generative UI components. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--generative_ui))
- `iteration_limit` (Number) Maximum number of agent loop iterations per run.
- `sandbox` (Attributes) Code execution sandbox for the agent. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--sandbox))

<a id="nestedatt--config--ask_user_questions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.ask_user_questions`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable this feature.


<a id="nestedatt--config--context_management"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.context_management`

Optional:

- `compaction` (Attributes) Conversation compaction. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--context_management--compaction))
- `large_tool_response` (Attributes) Offload large tool responses out of the context. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config--context_management--large_tool_response))

<a id="nestedatt--config--context_management--compaction"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.context_management.compaction`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable compaction.

Optional:

- `compaction_threshold_tokens` (Number) Token count above which the conversation is compacted.


<a id="nestedatt--config--context_management--large_tool_response"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.context_management.large_tool_response`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable this feature.



<a id="nestedatt--config--dynamic_sub_agents"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.dynamic_sub_agents`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable this feature.


<a id="nestedatt--config--generative_ui"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.generative_ui`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable this feature.


<a id="nestedatt--config--sandbox"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config.sandbox`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable the sandbox.

Optional:

- `file_downloads` (Boolean) Allow downloading files produced in the sandbox.



<a id="nestedatt--mcp_servers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mcp_servers`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the MCP server on the gateway.

Optional:

- `disable_tools` (List of String) Tools of this server the agent must not use. Accepts tool names and the `@all`, `@read`, `@write`, and `@destructive` groups.
- `enable_tools` (List of String) Tools of this server the agent may use. Accepts tool names and the `@all`, `@read`, `@write`, and `@destructive` groups.
- `preload` (Boolean) Load the server's tool list into the agent's context up front instead of on demand.
- `preload_tools` (List of String) Tools whose definitions are loaded up front. Accepts tool names and the `@all`, `@read`, `@write`, and `@destructive` groups.
- `require_approval_for_tools` (List of String) Tools that require human approval before each call. Accepts tool names and the `@all`, `@read`, `@write`, and `@destructive` groups.


<a id="nestedatt--response_format"></a>
### Nested Schema for `response_format`

Required:

- `type` (String) Response format: `text`, `json_schema` (structured output), or `json_object`.

Optional:

- `json_schema` (Attributes) JSON schema of the response (type `json_schema`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--response_format--json_schema))

<a id="nestedatt--response_format--json_schema"></a>
### Nested Schema for `response_format.json_schema`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the schema.

Optional:

- `description` (String) What the response contains.
- `schema` (String) The JSON schema as a JSON string, e.g. via jsonencode().
- `strict` (Boolean) Enforce the schema strictly.



<a id="nestedatt--sample_inputs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `sample_inputs`

Optional:

- `text` (String) Example user message.
- `variables` (Map of String) Variable values for this example.


<a id="nestedatt--skills"></a>
### Nested Schema for `skills`

Required:

- `fqn` (String) FQN of the agent skill.
- `preload` (Boolean) Load the skill's content into the agent's context up front instead of on demand.


<a id="nestedatt--variables"></a>
### Nested Schema for `variables`

Optional:

- `default_value` (String) Value used when the caller does not provide one.
- `description` (String) What the variable means.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Agents are imported by their name.
terraform import truefoundry_agent.support_triage support-triage
```
